correctness.rationale: The coefficient and exact update are algebraic least-squares identities. Gaussian sum/difference makes the numerator h independent of nondegenerate denominator D, whose density is positive at zero. Polar integrals prove the full sharp q<d moment cutoff, including failure at q=d. Ridge mean-square asymptotics derive from exact squared-ratio radial integrals and a uniformly L2-bounded remainder; d>=3 follows by dominated convergence. The 806 checks in the embedded verifier corroborate only identities and finite-ridge coefficients, not infinite-dimensional logic or priority.

value.rationale: Mean-square performance is a standard diagnostic for noisy numerical fixed-point solvers. This theorem proves an exact and consequential dimension-two boundary: even light-tailed oracle error induces infinite output MSE when a basic unsafeguarded depth-one Anderson step divides by a small residual difference. It further quantifies the precise penalty-cost scaling needed to suppress that singularity and contrasts dimensions one, two and at least three. This is more than a normalized sign/one-parameter example; it gives the complete moment regime for every fixed pair of distinct snapshots and precise leading constants.
